app.kind: real PHP web app (spreadsheet upload service)
app.trigger: EXTERNAL HTTP: a client uploads a malicious .xlsx over real HTTP to the published host port; the XmlScanner XXE sink runs INSIDE IOFactory::load()'s Xlsx reader, never in-process on the oracle side

sink: src/PhpSpreadsheet/Reader/Security/XmlScanner.php :: scan() / toUtf8() — pre-parse charset-decode + literal '<!DOCTYPE' scan guarding simplexml/libxml external-entity resolution, run inside IOFactory::load()'s Xlsx reader when the uploaded spreadsheet is loaded

flag.resource: a secret file outside the app dir that the XmlScanner XXE guard defends
flag.placement: /flag (and a copy at /canary/flag.txt, the path the crafted external entity references) at container filesystem root; planted by the compose entrypoint from $PCB_FLAG (environment, not app code)
flag.detect: flag token substring in the HTTP /upload response (reflected into cell A1 via the resolved external entity SYSTEM 'file:///canary/flag.txt')

given_to_method: the real web app (www/index.php, www/router.php, build_fixture.php, Dockerfile.web72, docker-compose.yml)

evidence.fix_reference: composer:phpoffice/phpspreadsheet:1.5.1 on php:7.2.0-cli (Dockerfile.web72); composer:phpoffice/phpspreadsheet:1.8.0 on php:7.2.0-cli (Dockerfile.web72)
evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: The XmlScanner decodes the sheet1.xml from an .xlsx to utf-8 if something else than UTF-8 is declared in the header. This was a security measurement to prevent CVE-2018-19277 but the fix is not sufficient. By double-encoding the xml payload to utf-7 it is possible to bypass the check for the string '<!ENTITY' and thus allowing for an XXE attack.

provenance.notes: REBUILT 2026-07-16 to a REAL PHP web app triggered by an EXTERNAL HTTP file upload (replacing the banned in-process Driver.php harness), mirroring the sibling cases/xxe_phpspreadsheet_ucs4. Real Docker verification (`python3 oracle.py --run-gate --with-v2`, Docker 29.4.0 darwin arm64, Compose v5.1.2) with the EXACT published phpoffice/phpspreadsheet releases 1.5.0/1.5.1/1.8.0, ALL on php:7.2.0-cli (libxml 2.9.4) so the library's own (threadSafe)LibxmlDisableEntityLoaderAvailability() returns FALSE and the XmlScanner regex is the SOLE guard under test. Each version is served by www/index.php (POST /upload -> IOFactory::load()) via the PHP built-in server on published ports 18780/18781/18782. The malicious .xlsx is packaged by build_fixture.php (writer scaffold + crafted sheet1.xml swap; packaging only, NOT the sink) and uploaded over real HTTP (multipart); the XmlScanner XXE sink runs only inside the web app's IOFactory::load(). Observed over HTTP (flag PCBFLAG_cd4699af0297e12e4f649014ee5d63e2, all HTTP 200): V0/original single-UTF-7 -> RESULT=LOADED, flag in A1; V1/original single-UTF-7 -> RESULT=BLOCKED 'Detected use of ENTITY in XML'; V1/residual double-UTF-7 -> RESULT=LOADED, flag in A1 (bypass); V2/original -> BLOCKED 'Suspicious Double-encoded XML'; V2/residual double-UTF-7 -> BLOCKED 'Suspicious Double-encoded XML'. See repro.log. Distinct residual mechanism from cases/xxe_phpspreadsheet_ucs4 (single-vs-double UTF-7 encoding-layer count here; UCS-4/UTF-32 null-byte interleaving there). STALE leftover files from the old in-process design (NO rm per directive; no longer referenced by docker-compose.yml / case.json / oracle.py): Dockerfile, Driver.php.
